name: Question 10
problem:
Consider the following differential equation

$$
{y}^{″}+2{y}^{′}+2y={e}^{-x}\operatorname{sec}⁡x.
$$

The general solution to this equation can be written as

$$
y(x)={e}^{-x}(A\operatorname{cos}⁡x+B\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+g(x),
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are constants. Which of the following could be the function $g(x)?$

*Hint: Use the variation of parameters method. You may also wish to make use of the following result (integration constant omitted):*

$$
\int \operatorname{tan}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{ln}⁡|\operatorname{cos}⁡x|
$$

Question 10
?

Consider the following differential equation y″+2y′+2y=e−xsec⁡x.

The general solution to this equation can be written as y(x)=e−x(Acos⁡x+Bsin⁡x)+g(x), where A and B are constants. Which of the following could be the function g(x)?

Hint: Use the variation of parameters method. You may also wish to make use of the following result (integration constant omitted): ∫tan⁡xdx=−ln⁡|cos⁡x|

a
e−x(cos⁡xln⁡|cos⁡x|−xsin⁡x)
b
e−x(sin⁡xln⁡|cos⁡x|+xcos⁡x)
c
xe−x(sin⁡xln⁡|cos⁡x|−xcos⁡x)
d
xe−x(cos⁡xln⁡|cos⁡x|+xsin⁡x)
e
e−x(cos⁡xln⁡|cos⁡x|+xsin⁡x)
Submit
